subject: Customer-controlled infrastructure: SLA liability summary & fallback play
messages:
From: Jordan Peters <jordan.peters@cascade-analytics.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarification on SLA carveout for our colo edge appliances

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. As we scope the Private deployment, legal and our infra team have flagged the need for an explicit SLA carveout for colo/edge equipment that Cascade controls (cross-connects, on-prem NAT, local load balancers).

Specifically:
- We control the WAN path past our demarc; any latency/outage attributable to that segment will be outside Redwood's responsibility.
- We need stated fallback behavior when the private link fails (automated failover to Redwood Hosted API is acceptable but we need details on expected latency/throughput change and any data residency implications).
- Please propose sample contract language and a credit calculation for availability impacts that are within Redwood's control.

Can you put together an operational ownership matrix + a short fallback play so procurement can sign off? We want to avoid a lengthy redline cycle.

Jordan
Senior Cloud Ops
Cascade Analytics

(Attached: none)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Peters <jordan.peters@cascade-analytics.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-22T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on SLA carveout for our colo edge appliances

Jordan — thanks, this is exactly the sort of clarity we want up front. I pulled together an initial operational responsibility matrix (attached) and a concise fallback play for the hosted fallback you mentioned. High level:

- Redwood responsibility: inference runtime, model-serving fleet, KV/prefix caching inside the private VPC, orchestration and health checks up to the private peering endpoint.
- Customer responsibility (Cascade): physical cross-connect, customer edge firewall/NAT, customer-managed load balancing, and any third-party transit beyond the demarc.

Fallback play (one-line): if private peering fails for >30s and autoscale cannot reestablish within 2m, route requests to Redwood Hosted API in the same region; degrade to the pinned model variant (quantized) to maintain cold-start latency targets. Expect median latency to increase by ~70–120ms depending on payloads.

Attached: proposed-resp-matrix.xlsx (ownership matrix + sample clause rows).

Next steps: 
1) Karhi/Marcus — can you draft the recommended contractual wording and credit formula we can present to Cascade procurement?
2) Jordan — confirm the exact demarc device hostname and emergency contact for your colo provider so we can record SRE playbook steps.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Account Lead — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
(attachment: proposed-resp-matrix.xlsx)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Jordan Peters <jordan.peters@cascade-analytics.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-23T08:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on SLA carveout for our colo edge appliances

On Mon, Apr 22, 2028 at 10:03 AM Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Jordan — thanks, this is exactly the sort of clarity we want up front. I pulled together an initial operational responsibility matrix (attached) and a concise fallback play for the hosted fallback you mentioned.

Thanks — adding proposed contract language and operational credit mechanics below (draft):

1) Service Availability SLO (Redwood-controlled components): Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide 99.95% monthly availability for the inference service endpoints and model-serving runtime within the customer VPC up to the Redwood-managed peering endpoint.

2) Excluded causes: Any unavailability or latency degradation caused by: (a) customer-managed cross-connect, firewall/NAT, or load balancer; (b) third-party transit providers outside the Redwood demarc; (c) interruptions initiated by customer admin actions — will be excluded from SLA calculations.

3) Credit calculation (example): When an eligible monthly availability breach occurs, credits will be computed as a percentage of monthly service fees: 0.5% credit for each 30 minutes below the SLA up to 10% per month. No credits apply for outages attributable to excluded causes.

4) Fallback behavior (operational): Redwood will provide an automated routing fallback to the Redwood Hosted API. During fallback: (i) requests are served by the pinned model variant; (ii) throughput is limited to the hosted product tier equivalent; (iii) data is processed according to the Hosted API T&Cs (linked in playbook).

Operational note: we should add a short-running health-probe on the customer demarc so both SREs get immediate alerts. Also recommend a signed 30-day playbook and a one-time failover dry-run during onboarding.

Playbook link: https://docs.redwood.ai/playbooks/private-to-hosted-failover

Marcus — can you confirm acceptable latency ranges for fallback quantized model and whether we need a specific egress/data residency rider?

-Karthik
VP, Reliability & Security
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Peters <jordan.peters@cascade-analytics.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-24T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on SLA carveout for our colo edge appliances

On Tue, Apr 23, 2028 at 8:11 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks — adding proposed contract language and operational credit mechanics below (draft):

Tessa / Karthik — this is helpful and close to what procurement wants. A couple of asks before we send to legal: 

- Credit mechanics: Cascade needs a clearer "who calls the breach" process. If our monitoring shows degradation on our side of the demarc, we authorize a credit submission. If the issue is ambiguous, we want an impartial 3rd-party packet capture review to adjudicate. Is Redwood open to that?
- Data residency: our compliance team requires that during fallback to Hosted API, request payloads stay in-region (we're US-only). Can you confirm Hosted routing will honor regional constraints as part of the play?
- Timeline: can Redwood commit to an onboarding/implementation window (including a dry-run) within 30 days of contract signature?

If you can answer these three points, procurement will run the draft through legal.

Jordan

(attachment: none)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Peters <jordan.peters@cascade-analytics.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-24T17:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on SLA carveout for our colo edge appliances

Jordan — thanks, answers inline and next steps below.

- 3rd-party adjudication: yes, we can accept a neutral packet-capture review process for ambiguous incidents. We recommend a single independent auditor selected jointly and scoping only the relevant time window for the incident.
- Regional routing for fallback: confirmed. Our Hosted API routing will honor the region constraint (US regional cluster) during fallback; we'll include a regional routing clause in the amendment.
- Timeline: Redwood can commit to a 30-day onboarding window post-signature for the fallback config and one scheduled dry-run failover (subject to mutually agreed blackout windows).

I've attached a short draft amendment for review (draft-amendment-custinfra.pdf) which includes the exclusion language, credit formula, neutral adjudicator clause, and a scheduling appendix for the dry-run. If Cascade is comfortable, we'll open a DocuSign for signature and schedule the dry-run with our SREs.

DocuSign (draft): https://app.docusign.com/embedded/sign/ABC123-cascade-amend

Please confirm final signers and any changes you want to the credit tiers.

Best regards,
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Account Lead — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
(attachment: draft-amendment-custinfra.pdf)
